title: metrics.py: start-time prune drops delayed latency; dedup/CSV sets unbounded
description:
## Problem

`Metrics` memory handling is incomplete in both directions, and the one prune it has destroys the latency samples that LatencyRule / SLA checks need.

### 1. `_tx_start_times` prune drops in-flight and delayed latency

`record_transmission_start` deletes start times older than `_TX_START_TIMES_MAX_AGE_US` (60s) once the dict exceeds `_TX_START_TIMES_PRUNE_THRESHOLD` (1000). Prune is by start-time age, not "already delivered."

`record_reception` then hits `start is None` and **silently skips latency** (same path as `test_reception_without_known_tx_has_no_latency`). Reception still counts. `latency_stats().count` lags `receptions`. Long-tail / LatencyRule / store-and-forward delays are exactly the samples that age past 60s.

SF10 ~4 TX/s/node; 10 nodes exceed 1000 TX inside 60s. City-mesh and chaos runs will prune. A 90s hop is counted as a success with no latency — `CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US` never sees it. This is the metrics-side hole 9098.14 found in the harness: catastrophic delay is sampled as "no latency," not a bound violation.

### 2. Dedup and CSV series are uncapped

The class already caps packet hashes (10k), latency samples (10k, reservoir), and dashboard series (300). It does **not** cap:

- `_delivered: set[tuple[str,str]]` — one entry per successful (rx, tx) forever (idempotency)
- `_collision_keys: set[tuple[str, frozenset[str]]]` — same for collisions
- `_time_series: list[...]` — every reception (and collision-with-time_us) forever for `export_csv`

Long-running sims grow without bound. Dashboard series was capped for this reason; the recording path used by `radio.py` was not.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (`record_transmission_start` prune, `record_reception` missing-start, `_delivered` / `_collision_keys` / `_time_series`)
- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (only production caller)
- python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py (`test_tx_start_times_pruned_after_threshold` asserts old keys vanish; does not then `record_reception` on a pruned id)

## Why this is robustness

Resource cleanup is the stated reason for the 60s prune, but that cleanup invalidates latency under load — the failure mode the prune was supposed to keep the process alive to measure. Unbounded dedup/CSV sets will OOM the same long runs. Operators sizing OSCORE/EDHOC timeouts from `latency_stats()` get a truncated distribution that hides the tail.
design: Do not prune a tx_id from _tx_start_times until its deliveries have been recorded or a fail-closed TTL after end_time+added has passed. Age _delivered / _collision_keys with the same TTL so polling idempotency survives the RX window without keeping keys forever. Cap _time_series like MetricsTimeSeries (deque maxlen) or drop events older than the dashboard window. A reception whose start time is gone must not look like a 0-latency success: either keep the start time or record latency as missing *and* surface it (do not increment receptions without a diagnostic).
acceptance_criteria: After >1000 TX starts, a reception 90s after tx start still records latency >= 90s (not a silent skip). latency_stats().count matches receptions for those deliveries. A long run of N deliveries does not grow _delivered / _time_series without bound (cap or TTL). test_tx_start_times_pruned_after_threshold still limits memory but no longer implies pruned ids lose later latency.
close_reason: Keep undelivered TX start times for 180s so 90s delayed RX still records latency; cap _delivered/_collision_keys/_time_series; receptions use a counter so caps do not shrink totals.
